ib/ma_announced.title: Announced M&A deal value
ib/ma_announced.why: Dollar value of announced global M&A. Deals are announced months before close, locking in advisory and financing fees well ahead of reported revenue — announcements are the industry's clearest forward pipeline measure, and announcement droughts mark the bottom of the fee cycle.
ib/ma_announced.source: PitchBook Global M&A Reports (free PDFs) — pitchbook.com/news/reports
ib/ma_announced.note: Annual values only: PitchBook's quarterly chart data carry no extractable text labels, and Dealogic's free PDFs yielded just 2 usable observations — this is a low-frequency backstop, not a pulse. Includes PitchBook estimates for late-reporting/nondisclosed deals. 2014 from the Q3 2024 report; 2015-2025 from the 2025 annual (latest-vintage-wins on restatement).

ib/ipo_pipeline.title: IPO pipeline — S-1 filing counts
ib/ipo_pipeline.why: Weekly count of initial Form S-1 registration statements on EDGAR. Registration precedes pricing by ~1-3 months, so filing counts signal ECM fee flow before it books; filing droughts are the earliest sign of a closed issuance window.
ib/ipo_pipeline.source: SEC EDGAR quarterly master indexes — sec.gov/edgar
ib/ipo_pipeline.note: Counts accessions, not dollar values — a SPAC and a mega-IPO each count once. Covers IPOs, SPACs, follow-ons and selling-shareholder registrations filed on S-1 (amendments excluded); F-1s (foreign private issuers) are a known gap.

ib/hy_issuance.title: High-yield bond issuance
ib/hy_issuance.why: US high-yield bond issuance per quarter. HY windows open and shut with risk appetite: issuance shutdowns precede DCM fee droughts and mark the turning points of the credit-risk-appetite cycle before spreads fully reprice.
ib/hy_issuance.source: SIFMA Research quarterly Fixed Income reports — sifma.org/research
ib/hy_issuance.note: Computed as SIFMA quarterly corporate issuance × HY share by type — SIFMA publishes no monthly HY series and its monthly workbook is form-gated, so this is a proxied quarterly read. Unpublished months are absent, never estimated.

ib/ib_fee_wallet.title: IB fee league-table trackers
ib/ib_fee_wallet.why: Quarterly IB fee wallet estimates from announced and completed deals — the industry's revenue line, published weeks before banks' quarterly filings.
ib/ib_fee_wallet.source: LSEG Deals Intelligence quarterly IB Review
ib/ib_fee_wallet.note: LSEG's quarterly fee decks are UUID-addressed with no stable archive; no buildable public series exists. Kept pending honestly rather than charted from an unarchivable feed.

ficc/move_index.title: MOVE proxy — 21d realized vol of 10Y yield
ficc/move_index.why: One-month Treasury-yield volatility reprices ahead of policy surprises and duration-driven deleveraging — the rates desk's fear gauge. This is the public proxy: annualized 21-trading-day realized volatility of the 10Y constant-maturity yield.
ficc/move_index.source: Computed: 21d realized vol of FRED DGS10 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
ficc/move_index.note: Realized, not implied: it measures what happened, omitting the volatility risk premium, and uses a single 10Y tenor vs the licensed ICE BofA MOVE index's 2Y-30Y swaption strip (no free MOVE series exists). Watch changes rather than levels.

ficc/hy_oas.title: US High Yield OAS
ficc/hy_oas.why: Option-adjusted spread of the US high-yield index over Treasuries — the market's real-time price of default and liquidity risk in lower-grade credit. HY spreads turn months before realized defaults (wide into 2007-08, March 2020, the 2022 hiking cycle).
ficc/hy_oas.note: Index OAS, not a traded spread: embeds a liquidity premium, so levels overstate pure default risk. FRED's ICE BofA cuts carry only a rolling 3-year window (history starts 2023-10). Read jointly with IG OAS — the HY-minus-IG slope is the risk-appetite read.

ficc/ig_oas.title: US Investment Grade OAS
ficc/ig_oas.why: Option-adjusted spread of the US investment-grade corporate index — the funding cost of the core of the credit market. IG spreads widen with systemic stress before defaults print; the BBB cohort is the cycle's pressure point (fallen-angel risk in a downturn).
ficc/ig_oas.note: Index OAS with liquidity premia; FRED's rolling 3-year window starts 2023-10. The companion to HY OAS above.

ficc/mbs_spread.title: Agency MBS spread (30Y mortgage − 30Y Treasury)
ficc/mbs_spread.why: The 30Y mortgage rate minus the 30Y Treasury yield — the agency-MBS spread. Widening signals dealer balance-sheet constraints and convexity-hedging pressure (the 2022 UK gilts/DHB lesson) before broad funding stress appears elsewhere.
ficc/mbs_spread.source: Computed: FRED OBMMIC30YF minus DGS30 — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/OBMMIC30YF
ficc/mbs_spread.note: The mortgage leg is the OBMMI 30Y fixed rate, not a traded security price — the spread embeds origination margins and mix, not pure MBS risk. Levels are structurally wider than traded MBS OAS; read changes.

ficc/wti_spot.title: WTI crude spot
ficc/wti_spot.why: WTI spot crude — the real-economy demand signal orthogonal to the heat map's price/stock quarterly metrics. Energy shocks feed inflation expectations and headline risk directly; the level is the dashboard's commodity anchor.
ficc/wti_spot.note: Spot only: the term-structure shape needs a futures curve and is charted separately as the WTI calendar spread in the cross-market segment.

ficc/sloos_tightening.title: SLOOS net % tightening C&I standards
ficc/sloos_tightening.why: Net percentage of US banks tightening commercial & industrial loan standards for large and midsize firms — the canonical credit-supply series. Tightening waves preceded the 1990, 2001, 2007-08 and 2022-23 downturns; Lown & Morgan (NY Fed Economic Policy Review, 2000) show loan growth slows substantially following reports of tighter standards. The single best public ex-ante read on bank credit supply.
ficc/sloos_tightening.source: FRED: DRTSCILM (Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey) — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DRTSCILM
ficc/sloos_tightening.frequency: Quarterly (~1 month after quarter-end; reflects prior quarter)
ficc/sloos_tightening.note: Diffusion measure — no magnitudes, and the reference quarter lags release by a quarter; occasional questionnaire breaks. Positive = net tightening; read direction and persistence, not the precise level. Charts from 1990Q2 (FRED coverage start).

ficc/cmi.title: NACM Credit Managers' Index (combined)
ficc/cmi.why: Monthly survey of B2B credit managers (manufacturing + services combined); 50 separates expansion from contraction. The credit function sees payment stress before delinquencies print — unfavorable factors slipping under 50 have preceded broader credit deterioration — making this the earliest private-credit read of each month (Aug 2026: 54.6, down 1.8 from July).
ficc/cmi.source: NACM Credit Managers' Index monthly reports — nacm.org
ficc/cmi.note: No FRED/API feed and unstable archive URLs: values are hand-transcribed from the monthly PDFs into data/pulse/manual/cmi.csv (README there documents the procedure and sources). Only verifiable months are charted — the series is intentionally sparse; gaps are never interpolated. Small panel, self-reported; the volatile dollar-sales component drives recent swings.

equities/put_call.title: CBOE equity put/call ratio
equities/put_call.why: Equity put/call ratio from CBOE daily statistics — options positioning's cleanest public read. Extremes flag crowded hedging or one-sided speculation roughly one to several weeks before price turns: low ratios mark complacency tops, spikes mark capitulation bottoms.
equities/put_call.note: Equity-only, total contract volume across all investor horizons — retail and dealer flow are indistinguishable. Historical CSV (frozen 2019-10-04) stitched to the daily publication page; definitions match exactly and were cross-checked at 7 dates.

equities/cape_zscore.title: Cyclically adjusted P/E vs 10-yr mean
equities/cape_zscore.why: Shiller CAPE as a z-score against its trailing 10-year mean. Starting valuation is the most robust medium-horizon return predictor in the equity literature — rich z-scores precede below-average long-run returns, though with notoriously loose timing.
equities/cape_zscore.source: Shiller CAPE via multpl.com (Yale ie_data.xls frozen) — multpl.com/shiller-pe
equities/cape_zscore.note: z = (CAPE − trailing 120m mean)/120m std. The Yale source file has been frozen since 2023-10-17, so values come from multpl.com's monthly republication. Mean-reversion timing risk: expensive can stay expensive for years.

equities/equity_issuance.title: US IPO + follow-on issuance volume
equities/equity_issuance.why: US IPO plus secondary issuance per quarter. Treasurers time equity supply to peak demand, so issuance surges cluster near cycle tops — a supply-side valuation signal that price-only gauges miss.
equities/equity_issuance.source: SIFMA Research quarterly reports (parsed PDFs) — sifma.org/research
equities/equity_issuance.note: IPOs + secondaries from SIFMA quarterly tables; newest-report-wins revision rule. SIFMA's monthly workbook is form-gated. Secondary offerings include selling-shareholder deals, so the series mixes issuer and holder motives.

equities/factor_rotation.title: High-beta minus low-vol 60-day relative strength
equities/factor_rotation.why: 60-day relative strength of high-beta vs low-volatility equities (SPHB − SPLV). Rotations into high-beta leadership mark late-cycle risk-appetite peaks; reversals into low-vol precede broad index turns as the marginal buyer defensive-shifts.
equities/factor_rotation.source: Yahoo Finance: SPHB, SPLV daily closes — finance.yahoo.com
equities/factor_rotation.note: 100 × (60d SPHB return − 60d SPLV return); positive = high-beta leading (risk-on). ETF-based, so index-construction changes bleed into both legs; the 60-day window smooths — read persistent swings, not single days.

equities/vvix.title: CBOE VVIX — volatility of volatility
equities/vvix.why: 30-day expected volatility of the VIX, implied from VIX options — the market's price of vol-regime instability, and the dashboard's vol-surface blind spot. Read by threshold, not level: VVIX above 120-140 flags vol-regime breaks (Feb 2018, March 2020 — VVIX turned up before VIX peaked); low VIX with low VVIX is the complacency mix that precedes disorderly unwinds.
equities/vvix.note: Not on FRED — ingested from CBOE's free CSV. Mean-reverting and itself volatile: compare against the 120-140 threshold band and its own history, never against other indices' scales. History from 2006-03.

awm/fund_flows.title: Net flows to long-term mutual funds & ETFs
awm/fund_flows.why: Net flows into long-term mutual funds and ETFs. Allocation shifts move AUM and fee bases weeks before reported revenue, and sustained redemptions are the observable footprint of risk-budget cuts — flows lead reported performance by a full reporting cycle.
awm/fund_flows.source: ICI statistical release workbooks (via public web archive) — ici.org
awm/fund_flows.note: Monthly actuals from ICI statistical-release workbooks via the public web archive; ICI's weekly release is a rolling 6-8 week window with no continuous public archive, so no weekly series is feasible — windows are never spliced.

awm/mmf_assets.title: Money-market fund total assets
awm/mmf_assets.why: Total money-market fund assets — the first stop of the risk-off cascade. Sharp inflows signal flight-to-cash and liquidity hoarding before equity redemptions and credit selling appear; the level is the system's cash reserve.
awm/mmf_assets.frequency: Quarterly (FRED's public cut of ICI's weekly data)
awm/mmf_assets.note: FRED's series is quarterly even though the underlying ICI release is weekly (weekly vintages sit behind ICI's form gate). A level, not a flow — read jumps, not the trend.

awm/sp500.title: S&P 500 level
awm/sp500.why: The S&P 500 level — the single beta that drives most AUM and fee-base change. Drawdowns lead AUM erosion and fee declines by a quarter or more; the level is the baseline against which every positioning gauge on this page is read.
awm/sp500.note: FRED's SP500 series carries only a rolling 10-year window; the pipeline refetches on each run and merges incrementally, so local history accumulates even as FRED drops its tail.

firmwide/cp_ois.title: 3M CP–bill spread (CP–OIS proxy)
firmwide/cp_ois.why: 3-month commercial paper minus the 3-month T-bill — the CP–OIS proxy. CP is the marginal unsecured funding market; spreads reprice within days as risk appetite erodes, the classic funding-stress lead (blew out in 2008 and March 2020 before equity vol peaked).
firmwide/cp_ois.source: Computed: FRED DCPN3M minus DGS3MO — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCPN3M
firmwide/cp_ois.note: CP-bill, the literature's funding-stress gauge: no public 3M OIS series exists, and SOFR-average OIS proxies were rejected (backward-looking staleness produced hiking-cycle artifacts larger than the COVID signal). AA financial CP leg.

firmwide/fra_ois.title: 1m-forward-2m CP–bill spread (FRA–OIS proxy)
firmwide/fra_ois.why: The 1-month-forward 2-month CP minus T-bill spread — the FRA–OIS proxy. It prices forward term-funding risk plus embedded bank counterparty credit, so it leads spot funding stress when dealers price deterioration ahead of it.
firmwide/fra_ois.source: Computed from FRED CP and T-bill rates — fred.stlouisfed.org
firmwide/fra_ois.note: Constructed from FRED CP and bill rates; the traded 3M×3M FRA and OIS legs have no public feed. A Treasury-implied-forward alternative was rejected (no bank-credit component; mis-signed in stress).

firmwide/margin_debt.title: FINRA margin debt (debit balances)
firmwide/margin_debt.why: Debit balances in customers' securities margin accounts (FINRA Rule 4521 statistics). Client leverage builds ahead of forced deleveraging; month-over-month contractions have preceded volatility cascades (2000, 2008, 2020) as the marginal buyer loses capacity.
firmwide/margin_debt.note: Aggregate across all FINRA-reporting firms. A level, not a ratio — the signal is rate-of-change; pair with equity levels for the leverage-cycle read.

firmwide/dealer_cds.title: Single-A corporate OAS (dealer CDS proxy)
firmwide/dealer_cds.why: Single-A US corporate OAS — the public proxy for average dealer senior CDS. Market-implied default intensity of the counterparty layer widens before CVA losses or rating actions; dealer stress is systemic stress (the 2008 insurer lesson).
firmwide/dealer_cds.note: No free CDS feed exists and FRED carries no US banking-sector ICE BofA OAS; US GSIB senior bonds cluster in single-A, but the bucket includes nonfinancial single-A issuers and all maturities ≥1Y, and OAS embeds liquidity premia. Rolling 3-year FRED window (history starts 2023-10) means no crisis backfill — compare changes, not absolute levels.

firmwide/nfci_credit.title: Chicago Fed NFCI — credit subindex
firmwide/nfci_credit.why: The credit-conditions block of the Chicago Fed's weekly 105-indicator financial-conditions composite (mean 0, sd 1; positive = tighter). It isolates the credit-tightening channel — bank and shadow-bank standards and spreads — that OAS levels alone miss; the NFCI family leads the Board's FCI-G growth-impact gauge (Brave & Butters, Chicago Fed Letter 2012). Rose through 2007 into 2008; spiked March 2020.
firmwide/nfci_credit.frequency: Weekly (Wednesday release for week ending Friday)
firmwide/nfci_credit.note: Principal-components construction: the entire history is recomputed and revised every week — compare vintages with care and don't archive-splice (the pipeline merges by date, keeping the latest vintage). Largely contemporaneous — a stress thermometer, not a forecast; some components are slow-moving.

plumbing/sofr_iorb.title: SOFR–IORB spread
plumbing/sofr_iorb.why: SOFR minus the interest-on-reserve-balances rate — the overnight secured-funding corridor's thermometer. When secured funding sits below the administered rate, reserves are abundant; a persistent move toward and above IORB flags reserve scarcity, the 2019 repo spike's ex-ante signature.
plumbing/sofr_iorb.note: IORB starts 2021-07-29 (predecessor administered-rate series are not comparable), which bounds the backfill. Daily noise around quarter-ends — read the trend.

plumbing/on_rrp.title: ON RRP take-up
plumbing/on_rrp.why: Cash parked in the Fed's overnight reverse repo facility is cash not funding markets. A collapse toward zero means reserves are no longer abundant — the 2024-25 drain — which is historically the plumbing precondition for funding-pressure episodes.
plumbing/on_rrp.note: The level reflects Treasury float, TGA changes and money-fund allocation power, not just stress; read jointly with the SOFR-IORB spread.

plumbing/dealer_fails.title: Primary dealer fails-to-deliver
plumbing/dealer_fails.why: Fails-to-deliver in Treasuries, summed across the NY Fed's 11 primary-dealer reporting series. Fails spike when settlement chains seize — the observable footprint of collateral scarcity and dealer balance-sheet constraint (2008, March 2020, crisis-level signatures).
plumbing/dealer_fails.note: Values suppressed below the confidentiality threshold (reported as "*") are treated as 0 — the true number is small but nonzero, so read extremes, not levels.

plumbing/fhlb.title: FHLB advances
plumbing/fhlb.why: Federal Home Loan Bank advances — banks' wholesale funding tap of first resort when deposits flee. Surges flag liquidity stress before it reaches the discount window; the 2023 regional-bank episode's emergency borrowings were FHLB-led.
plumbing/fhlb.source: FHLB Office of Finance Combined Financial Reports — fhlb-of.com
plumbing/fhlb.note: Parsed from CFR PDFs (MD&A advances figure). Older reports live under different URL paths the fetcher does not chase, so coverage is the quarters the current pattern reaches (2025Q2 onward as of 2026-10); unpublished quarters are skipped, never estimated.

plumbing/treasury_basis.title: Treasury cash–futures basis (proxy)
plumbing/treasury_basis.why: The cash-futures basis proxy: the cash 10Y yield minus the yield implied by the ZN futures price. A wider (more positive) basis means cash Treasuries cheapen relative to futures — the classic footprint of dealer balance-sheet constraint in the world's deepest market (2019 repo, March 2020).
plumbing/treasury_basis.source: Computed: FRED DGS10 minus Yahoo ZN=F implied yield — fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
plumbing/treasury_basis.note: Proxy: futures-implied yield of a hypothetical 6%-coupon 10-year note at the quoted price — abstracts from cheapest-to-deliver options, delivery timing, and repo financing. Yahoo's ZN=F is the front contract; roll artifacts possible around expiry. Compare changes, not levels.

plumbing/xccy_basis.title: EUR/USD cross-currency basis (CIP construction)
plumbing/xccy_basis.why: The EUR/USD cross-currency basis — a negative basis means synthetic dollars via EUR cost more than direct dollars, the offshore dollar-shortage thermometer (blew out in 2008 and 2011, the canonical dollar-stress episodes; covered-basis methodology per Du, Tepper & Verdelhan).
plumbing/xccy_basis.source: Constructed: CME Euro FX futures + FRED DEXUSEU, DGS3MO, IR3TIB01EZM156N — fred.stlouisfed.org
plumbing/xccy_basis.note: Experimental DIY construction; EUR leg only; series starts 2025-04 (Yahoo delists expired futures contracts). The FRED Euribor input is stale between fixings and the T-bill leg is not banks' marginal funding rate — watch changes, not levels.

positioning/cftc_cot.title: Speculative rate-futures z-scores
positioning/cftc_cot.why: Leveraged-fund net positioning in rate futures (UST 2Y/5Y/10Y notes, 3M SOFR), z-scored against its trailing 2-year window. Crowded positioning at extremes has preceded sharp rate repricings — the flip side of every rates-vol episode of the 2022-23 cycle.
positioning/cftc_cot.source: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures — cftc.gov/MarketReports
positioning/cftc_cot.note: Four contracts: leveraged-fund net (long − short) z-scored against the trailing 104-week window, current week excluded. Positioning ≠ price: extremes can persist; read as a fragility overlay, not a directional call.

positioning/etf_dislocation.title: Corporate bond ETF dislocation (proxy)
positioning/etf_dislocation.why: Corporate-bond ETF price vs its trailing 20-day mean (LQD, HYG). An ETF trading far below its own recent average is the observable footprint of a price/NAV dislocation — in March 2020 LQD and HYG traded at steep discounts that mean-reverted violently once dealer balance sheets freed up.
positioning/etf_dislocation.source: Yahoo Finance: LQD, HYG vs trailing 20-day mean — finance.yahoo.com
positioning/etf_dislocation.note: Proxy: (close − 20d MA)/20d MA — the true (market price − NAV)/NAV leg is not published in machine-readable form; labeled a proxy, not the accounting discount. The stress signature is a gap of roughly −2% or worse, not small daily wiggles.

positioning/cds_bond_basis.title: Excess Bond Premium (CDS–bond basis proxy)
positioning/cds_bond_basis.why: The Excess Bond Premium (Gilchrist–Zakrajšek methodology, FEDS Notes) — the non-default (liquidity/funding) component of corporate spreads, exactly what the CDS-bond basis measures (Bai & Collin-Dufresne, 2019). EBP spikes flag dealer-intermediation stress before defaults move; it led the 2007-08 widening.
positioning/cds_bond_basis.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Notes EBP series — federalreserve.gov
positioning/cds_bond_basis.note: The FEDS EBP stands in for the unobservable dealer-quoted basis; direction matches dealer-quoted basis (spikes when funding stress widens it), but levels are NOT comparable to dealer CDS quotes — compare deviations, not absolutes.

positioning/insider_selling.title: Bank insider net selling
positioning/insider_selling.why: Net open-market selling by officers and directors of the eight US GSIBs (SEC Form 4 filings via OpenInsider). Insiders sell ahead of bad news more reliably than they buy ahead of good — persistent net selling is the sector's quiet sentiment read.
positioning/insider_selling.source: OpenInsider (SEC Form 4 filings): JPM, BAC, C, WFC, GS, MS, USB, PNC — openinsider.com
positioning/insider_selling.note: Each ticker page lists only recent transactions, so the trailing ~12 months are the usable window; amendments and duplicates are not de-duplicated — treat the level as approximate and month-over-month changes as the signal. Motives are invisible: diversification is not information.

filings/htm_unrealized.title: Bank HTM unrealized losses
filings/htm_unrealized.why: Aggregate unrealized losses on banks' held-to-maturity securities — the unrealized-capital hole that forced sales crystallize. A rising stock of paper losses raises the probability that a deposit run forces realization: the SVB lesson in aggregate.
filings/htm_unrealized.note: Balance-sheet row 'Held to maturity on non-equity securities unrealized gain/loss', sign-flipped so positive values are losses. Aggregate level, not risk-weighted — pair with deposit outflows for the run-risk read.

filings/n_mfp.title: MMF repo counterparty concentration
filings/n_mfp.why: Top-3 dealer share of money-fund repo counterparties (SEC Form N-MFP filings). Repo is the marginal funding market — when a handful of dealers dominate it, a single counterparty wobble propagates; flow concentrated into fewer hands in the March 2020 dealer crunch.
filings/n_mfp.source: SEC DERA Form N-MFP monthly data sets — sec.gov
filings/n_mfp.note: Sponsored-repo rows are attributed to the named sponsor dealer and residual unmapped volume is excluded from the dealer ranking (top-3 share ≈ 27.13% under this methodology — supersedes an earlier 14.6% print that used a different attribution).

filings/earnings_calls.title: Bank earnings-call credit language
filings/earnings_calls.why: Credit-quality language in bank earnings calls (JPM, BAC, WFC), scored per 10k words. Management language on credit quality, reserves, and provisions shifts before charge-offs show up in the numbers; the v1 framework caught the actual Q3-2026 reserve build.
filings/earnings_calls.source: Motley Fool earnings-call transcripts (JPM, BAC, WFC) — fool.com
filings/earnings_calls.note: v1 methodology proof, not a production time series: no transcript harvester ships yet, so the pipeline charts the verified Q3-2026 calibration point (JPM 7.6 / BAC 11.6 / WFC 8.9 per 10k words) honestly rather than pretending a history.

crossmarket/wti_calendar_spread.title: WTI calendar spread (prompt−12M)
crossmarket/wti_calendar_spread.why: The WTI prompt-month futures price minus the contract ~12 months out. Backwardation (positive) means a tight physical market and low inventories; contango (negative) means glut. The curve's slope reprices inventories before spot does — the physical market's stress gauge.
crossmarket/wti_calendar_spread.source: Yahoo Finance: CL=F front month minus the contract expiring ~12 months later — finance.yahoo.com
crossmarket/wti_calendar_spread.note: Yahoo delists expired contracts, so the 12M leg exists only where the contract is still listed — trailing ~12 months of history. Roll timing adds noise around expiry weeks.

sentiment/epu_daily.title: Economic Policy Uncertainty — daily news index
sentiment/epu_daily.why: Scaled frequency of newspaper articles about economic policy uncertainty across major US papers (Baker, Bloom & Davis, QJE 2016). EPU innovations foreshadow declines in investment, employment and output — uncertainty shocks act like negative demand shocks. Spiked into Lehman, the 2011 debt-ceiling standoff, the 2016 election, March 2020, and the 2025 tariff round.
sentiment/epu_daily.note: News-based, so partly endogenous — it reacts to events rather than pricing them ex ante — and noisy at daily frequency; the literature smooths 7-30 days. The monthly composite (USEPUINDXM) mixes in slow components (tax-code expirations, forecaster disagreement), so the daily news count is the purer pulse.

sentiment/news_sentiment.title: SF Fed Daily News Sentiment
sentiment/news_sentiment.why: Lexical sentiment of economics-related news across 24 major US newspapers (Factiva), aggregated daily with geometrically declining weights (Shapiro, Sudhof & Wilson, J. Econometrics 2022). It fell sharply in January 2020, ~2 months before the Michigan and Conference Board measures moved — a real-time nowcast of soft data.
sentiment/news_sentiment.note: Publication is weekly, so the tail always lags several days — the pipeline charts exactly what the file contains and never fabricates unpublished days. Lexicon-based: it reads economics sentiment broadly, not financial stress specifically, and can misread novel contexts.

sentiment/gpr_threats.title: Geopolitical Risk — threats subindex (GPT)
sentiment/gpr_threats.why: Share of newspaper articles covering adverse geopolitical events across 10 US/UK/Canadian papers — threats only (statements of risk before anything happens; Caldara & Iacoviello, AER 2022). Threats build before acts — a genuine ex-ante lead: GPR shocks depress investment and employment and lift VIX and credit spreads (9/11, 2003 Iraq, 2014 and 2022 Russia-Ukraine, the 2026 Iran conflict).
sentiment/gpr_threats.note: Western-press perspective — local-language indices can diverge materially (Bondarenko et al., 2024); fixed keyword lists can miss novel risks. Threats (GPT) is charted rather than acts (GPA) because the dashboard's mandate is leading, not coincident, risk. A daily file exists but carries only a short recent window, so the monthly series is the stable one.

sentiment/cfo_optimism.title: CFO Survey — economic optimism index
sentiment/cfo_optimism.why: Quarterly optimism of ~400-550 US CFOs about the economy (0-100), from The CFO Survey (Duke Fuqua with the Richmond and Atlanta Feds; long Graham-Harvey survey lineage). CFO expectations lead capex, hiring and issuance; optimism fell 66.0→62.1 in 2025Q1 on tariff fears and read 60.3 in 2026Q3 with 20% of small firms financially constrained — a forward read on corporate demand for IB services and credit.
sentiment/cfo_optimism.source: The CFO Survey press releases — fuqua.duke.edu/duke-fuqua-insights/
sentiment/cfo_optimism.note: No machine feed: values are hand-transcribed from quarterly releases into data/pulse/manual/cfo_optimism.csv (README documents the procedure). Gaps stay gaps — 2025Q2 and the first half of 2026 are absent because those releases state no numeric index in their public text. Quarterly, modest sample, optimism-level bias; C-suite sentiment, not market pricing.
